title: How to open a turnkey café or restaurant: from concept to launch
seo_title: Turnkey Restaurant Fit-Out: From Concept to Launch
description: Opening a café or restaurant turnkey: concept, premises, interior design, renovation, furniture from China and launch — the order of steps and the budget.
lead: Opening a café or restaurant turnkey means getting from idea to first guest without chaos between the designer, the builders and the suppliers. Here is the order to follow, what to check before you sign a lease and what a venue budget is made of.
photo_alt: Restaurant dining room with round tables under arches and a timber ceiling — Yacht Restaurant design project
body: Start with the concept, not the renovation

The most expensive mistake a venue owner can make is starting the renovation before it is clear what exactly is opening. A takeaway coffee shop, a breakfast café, a full-kitchen restaurant and a cocktail bar are different premises, different building services and different furniture. So the first document is not an estimate but a short concept.

It only needs to answer a few questions. Who is your guest and how long do they stay? What is the menu and what does the kitchen need for it? How many covers do you want, and will there be a terrace? What atmosphere should people feel from the doorway? These answers later become the layout, lighting, materials and furniture specification.
format: coffee shop, café, restaurant, bar, hotel venue
menu and kitchen process: what you cook on site and what arrives ready
number of covers inside and on the terrace
mood and references: what you like in other venues
Premises: what to check before signing the lease

A great location with poor building services can eat the budget before you even open. Before signing a lease, show the premises to a designer or technical specialist: they will assess whether your concept fits and what it will cost to deliver.
allocated electrical capacity — is it enough for the kitchen equipment
whether ventilation and kitchen extraction can be routed out
water supply, drainage and space for a grease trap
ceiling height and room to conceal services
a separate entrance, fire exits and convenient deliveries
lease terms during the renovation period

If anything on this list is in doubt, find out before signing — not after the furniture has been ordered. Sometimes a small change to the concept, such as a kitchen without open flame, makes difficult premises perfectly workable.
Interior design for a café or restaurant

Interior design for a venue is about operations first and beauty second. We start with flows: how guests enter and wait, how waiters carry plates, where staff change, how goods are delivered. Guest and staff flows must not cross where that gets in the way of service.

Then comes the interior concept, 3D visualisations, working drawings and the specification: every material, piece of furniture and light fitting with product codes and quantities. That specification becomes the basis for the renovation estimate and the procurement order. More about this stage on our [restaurant and café design](/en/restaurant-design) page.

Lighting is planned separately. In a venue it works in several scenes: daytime, evening, events. Ideally scenes switch with one button, and the light over a table shows off the plate rather than dazzling the guest.
Communal table with mismatched chairs, chandeliers and a wine wall in the Monpark restaurant dining room
Monpark: a communal table and wine wall as part of the dining room concept

A venue renovation differs from an apartment renovation in the amount of building services. Ventilation and air conditioning, electrics for kitchen equipment, water supply, drainage, sound insulation from the neighbours — all of this is installed before finishing and has to match the drawings to the centimetre.

Materials are chosen for heavy use: flooring that withstands daily wet cleaning, walls by the tables that will not mind chair scuffs, bar tops resistant to moisture and alcohol. A beautiful but impractical material in a venue quickly becomes a reason for another renovation.

Control matters during the works: photo reports every 1–2 weeks, inspection of concealed works before walls are closed, compliance with the design. When the renovation is run by the same team that did the design, decisions on site are made faster.

Procurement is often the largest part of the budget after the renovation. Dining chairs and tables, sofas, bar stools, terrace furniture, decorative and technical lighting, tableware, glassware, textiles, bathroom accessories — dozens of items that have to match each other and arrive on time.

A large share of these items is worth sourcing directly from factories in China. In our catalogue, [Ozdoba (in Ukrainian)](/ozdoba), the minimum order starts at $500; items can be combined, and we do not sell single pieces because we furnish whole properties. Delivery takes 30–60 days, so we order right after the specification is approved, in parallel with the renovation.

A venue budget has several parts: design project, renovation with building services, furniture and lighting, kitchen equipment and launch. Our interior design costs from $30 per m², with a minimum project fee of $2,500. For a 120 m² venue, for example, design starts from 120 × $30 = $3,600.

We price a café or restaurant renovation from the design: the cost depends heavily on the condition of the premises, ventilation, kitchen and the chosen materials. Procurement from the Ozdoba catalogue can start from $500. If CAS carries out the renovation to our design, the final figure stays within ±5% of the approved estimate — so you can plan the opening without surprises.
Tip: keep a reserve for changes that appear during launch — extra kitchen shelving, different lighting over the bar, a few more chairs for the terrace.

Once the renovation is done and the furniture has arrived, it is time for assembly and placement, equipment connection, lighting and decor installation, lighting scene set-up and cleaning. Then the dining room is styled, so the venue is ready both for its first guests and for a social media photo shoot.

Before opening, run a soft-launch day for friends. Staff test their routes, the kitchen tests the equipment, and you see whether guests are comfortable, whether there is enough light and whether the music is too loud. Small fixes made before opening cost far less than rework in a venue that is already serving guests every day.

faq: Where do I start when opening a café or restaurant?
With the concept: format, menu, number of covers and atmosphere. Then come the premises check before leasing, the design project, renovation, procurement and launch.
How much does restaurant interior design cost?
From $30 per m², with a minimum project fee of $2,500. For a 120 m² dining room that is from $3,600. Renovation is priced from the estimate after the design.
How long does furniture from China take?
Delivery takes 30–60 days, so we order right after the specification is approved, in parallel with the renovation.
Can I order only the furnishing of my venue?
Yes. We can furnish your venue to your own design. The minimum order in the Ozdoba catalogue is from $500, and items can be combined.
